# Kessel 0.9.0 — Privacy, Media & Phones
Kessel 0.9.0 adds privacy and security controls, extensions, a side panel with workspaces and an AI assistant, media controls and graphics settings to the desktop browser. It is also the first release of **Kessel for phones**, the Android app.

## What's new on the desktop
- **Privacy:**
  - A cookie viewer and editor, and per-site cookie rules: allow, keep until Kessel closes, or block. You can also cap how long any cookie is kept.
  - Other sites' cookies inside a page are refused by default. Partitioned cookies still work.
  - Delete one site's data (cookies, storage, caches, service workers). Clear chosen data when Kessel quits.
  - "Always use private windows."
  - Global Privacy Control (on by default) and Do Not Track.
  - Choose the referrer policy and what Kessel tells sites it is.
  - Click-tracking redirect pages (google.com/url, l.facebook.com…) are skipped.
  - More fingerprinting protection: WebGL and screen size, plus an optional UTC time zone.
- **Security:**
  - The URLhaus, phishing and uBlock badware lists: a dangerous site gets a warning page, whether Shields is on or not.
  - HTTPS-only mode, warning pages for certificate errors, and "Not secure" on http sites.
  - The lock in the address bar opens the site's info: the connection, its certificate, its cookies, and a button to clear its data.
  - Risky downloads wait until you keep or discard them. Microsoft Defender SmartScreen is available as an opt-in.
  - Extensions the Chrome Web Store removed as malware are turned off.
- **Extensions:**
  - Install from the Chrome Web Store or Edge Add-ons ("Add to Kessel"), from a .crx/.zip file, or unpacked.
  - Turn them on and off, remove them, choose their site access, and let them update themselves. There's a developer mode too.
  - The puzzle button in the address bar opens their popups, and their side-panel pages open in Kessel's side panel.
  - Blockers built on `declarativeNetRequest` (such as uBlock Origin Lite) install, but the engine doesn't apply their rules. Shields does that job instead.
- **Side panel and workspaces:**
  - The side panel has bookmarks, a reading list, history, notes, search, workspaces and extensions.
  - An AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity, Le Chat or your own) sits in the side panel. Right-click a page for "Ask AI about this".
  - Workspaces: each window shows one workspace's tabs, and the others sleep until you switch back.
- **Media controls:** the music-note button beside the menu appears once a tab plays sound. For any tab in the window, without switching to it, you can:
  - play, pause and seek
  - skip back or ahead 10 seconds, or to the previous/next track
  - change the speed
  - choose captions or an audio track
  - pop the video out into picture-in-picture
- **Hardware acceleration:** Settings → Performance can turn it off, and pick which graphics card Kessel uses: automatic (the power-saving one when Kessel starts on battery), power-saving or high-performance.
- **`kessel://gpu`:** what the graphics card does for Kessel (renderer, WebGL, WebGPU, HDR and wide colour) and which video and audio formats play and are decoded in hardware. It includes a "Copy report" button.
- **Settings → All features:** every feature and how to use it, searchable.
- **Also:**
  - Windows dragged in from other browsers bring every tab, including Edge's, with full addresses. The other browser's window only closes once all its tabs are read, and drops register faster.
  - Shields no longer inspects requests while it's switched off.
  - Upgrading a site to HTTPS falls back to http when it has to.
- The feature checklist ([FEATURES.md](https://github.com/puss-in-boots-org/kessel-browser/blob/main/FEATURES.md)) now opens with a progress table: 43% of 1,025 items.

## New: Kessel for phones (Android)
The same browser, laid out for one hand. Its source is in [`kessel-mobile/`](https://github.com/puss-in-boots-org/kessel-browser/tree/main/kessel-mobile).
- **Address bar at the bottom** (or the top), with the desktop's suggestions and instant answers: calculator, units, currencies, definitions. Swipe along it to change tabs.
- **Tab grid** with pictures of your tabs. Swipe a card to close it. Tabs you haven't looked at in a while sleep, and your tabs come back after a restart.
- **Private tabs** with their own cookies and storage, deleted when the last one closes.
- **Shields:** ad and tracking servers from EasyList, EasyPrivacy and Peter Lowe's list are blocked. Tracking parameters are removed from links, and you can turn Shields off for one site.
- Bookmarks, history, downloads, find in page, desktop site, share, add to home screen, and print or save as PDF.
- Long-press links and pictures to open, copy, share or download them.
- Fullscreen video that carries on in **picture-in-picture** when you leave Kessel.
- Camera, microphone and location only after you allow them. Pop-ups are blocked.
- Kessel can be your **default browser**, and it has "New tab" / "New private tab" shortcuts on its icon.
- Left on the desktop:
  - windows, split view and the side panel
  - the password vault and imports
  - extensions and keyboard shortcuts
  - the desktop's page-level Shields (element hiding, scriptlets, fingerprinting)

## Before you install
- **Windows:** the installers are not code-signed yet. Windows SmartScreen will warn you ("Windows protected your PC" → More info → Run anyway). On PCs with **Smart App Control** turned on, Windows blocks them outright. Requires Windows 10/11 with the WebView2 runtime, which comes preinstalled on current Windows.
- **Android:** Android 10 or later. Open the APK on your phone and allow your browser or file manager to install apps when Android asks.
  - Unless this repository has a release signing key set up, the APK is signed with a test key. A later release signed with a different key can't update it, so uninstall first.
  - Private tabs need a recent Android System WebView, which updates through the Play Store.
- **Not yet tried on a real device:**
  - The desktop's media controls, hardware-acceleration settings and `kessel://gpu` have unit tests and end-to-end tests, but those end-to-end tests haven't been run on Windows yet.
  - The Android app is built and unit-tested, but hasn't been tried on a phone yet.

  Please report anything that misbehaves.

## Downloads
- `Kessel_0.9.0_x64-setup.exe`: the Windows installer (recommended)
- `Kessel_0.9.0_x64_en-US.msi`: an MSI package for managed Windows installs
- `Kessel_0.9.0_android.apk`: Kessel for phones, to install directly
- `Kessel_0.9.0_android.aab`: an Android App Bundle, for Google Play
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`: checksums for verifying the downloads
